items.headline: Stocks Retreat from Record Highs on Weak Retail Sales
items.summary: U.S. equities concluded Friday, August 14, 2026, mostly lower, pulling back from recent record closes. Weaker-than-expected July retail sales data sparked concerns about consumer spending and economic growth, overshadowing earlier optimism from softer inflation reports that had eased fears of aggressive Federal Reserve rate hikes. Oil prices edged higher amid ongoing Middle East tensions. Not financial advice.

items.headline: Energy Sector Outperforms Amid Geopolitical Tensions; Healthcare Lags
items.summary: The energy sector was the top performer on Friday, gaining 1.36%, as elevated tensions in the Strait of Hormuz drove Brent crude prices higher. Conversely, the healthcare sector was the worst performer, falling 0.60%, as investors rotated towards energy stocks and major healthcare companies faced weakness. Data storage and memory stocks also saw strong performance during the week.

items.headline: U.S. Retail Sales Decline Unexpectedly in July
items.summary: U.S. retail sales unexpectedly fell 0.6% in July to $763.6 billion, marking the steepest drop since May 2025 and missing economists' forecasts for a 0.1% increase. This data raised concerns about the resilience of consumer spending and its potential impact on economic growth.

items.headline: PPI Unchanged, CPI Moderates; Fed Hike Fears Ease
items.summary: The Producer Price Index (PPI) remained unchanged month-over-month in July, coming in below expectations. This, coupled with a modest 0.1% rise in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) for July and a slight annual deceleration to 3.4%, helped to reduce investor concerns about further Federal Reserve interest rate hikes.

items.headline: Mixed Earnings Reports from Key Companies
items.summary: Boost Run Inc. ($BRUN) reported strong Q2 2026 revenue of $31.1 million, a 270% increase year-over-year. Parabolic (Banzai International, Inc., $PARA) reported a Q2 2026 net loss of $5.0 million on revenues of $2.3 million. Meanwhile, Applied Materials ($AMAT) saw its stock decline despite reporting strong earnings, as high market expectations for AI-related companies contributed to a sell-off.
